doc.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024

title: How his students make a living
summary: Few students live on playing alone; many teach, including one charging $125 an hour to adult hobbyists.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Ah yes. Did you ever play “Wipe Out” for tips?

Yeah, yeah. And my students now, the ones who are successful, very few are successful just playing drums. There’s so many other avenues that are necessary to — especially if they have families. Some of them become website builders. A lot of them have very lucrative teaching practices. I was talking to one of my former students who was a very inventive, creative individual but who supports his music by teaching. And he charges something like $125 an hour. And I say, “My God, do kids have that much money?” And he says, “Oh I’m not teaching kids.” I said, “Well who are you teaching?” “I’m teaching doctors, lawyers, stockbrokers, guys who go home and have drum dreams.”
Yes, they probably have the most expensive drum sets too.
Exactly. Yeah. Oh man, yeah. So I’m thinking right on, go for it, you know?
